newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power prices mixed ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power prices mixed ahead of holiday.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were on either side of unchanged Monday in another lackluster trading session, but most expected prices to rebound by early next week as industrial loads rise.
Temperatures throughout the Midwest are expected to moderate as the week progresses, reaching seven to 12 degrees above-normal by the end of the week.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were discussed in the $15.50-$16.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, down about 50 cents from Friday.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power for Tuesday was pegged at $10.00-$10.50.
Separately, the 420 megawatt (MW) Big Stone coal-fired generating plant in South Dakota, shut Thursday for repairs, is expected to resume service Tuesday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday slipped into the $16.00-17.00 range, as compared with Friday's trading range of $17.50-$20.00.
MAIN off peak power for Tuesday was assessed at $11.50-12.00, but no deals were confirmed done.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday were in the $13.00-14.00 range, little changed from Friday.
For Thursday/Friday delivery, peak, non-firm prices in ECAR were talked in the $15.00-16.00 area.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were quoted again at $11.00-$13.00.
Separately, Detroit Edison's 1,116 MW Fermi 2 nuclear unit in Newport, Mich., shut again this Saturday, is expected to restart later this week.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), where temperatures are expected to climb to as much as 20 degrees above-normal this week, peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were in the $11.00-$11.50 range, down from Friday's range of $13.50-$14.50.
These prices reflect much softer natural gas prices in Texas in the $2.60s per million British thermal units.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Tuesday delivery were still assessed around $12.00.
January/February peak prices in SPP were down in the $21.00-22.50 range, as compared with the $22.00-$23.00 range seen on Friday.
Despite these current weak values, most traders said they were anticipating an uptick in prices by early next week as industrial loads return to normal levels.
"I think you'll see reality return next week. Even if the weather isn't there, the holidays will be over," one market source said.
